edge_geometry_notes:
Sources for the shape: Sceptre's own product photos (GalleryZip product_id 1134/1362/1470, saved at C:\Users\seanr\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--repos-3d-skills\1d674529-f719-450b-a8ca-43a8facc5bb1\scratchpad\gallery\) and the rendered manual pages (…\scratchpad\pages\). Nothing below is a published number unless it says so.

FRONT / BEZEL. 'Edgeless' design: the glass runs to the housing edge on the top and both sides with a thin black border under it (retailer 8.0 mm, reviewer ~6.35 mm; inferred from housing width minus active width: 8-10 mm per side). The bottom is a conventional plastic chin carrying the SCEPTRE logo, visibly wider than the top/sides (not published; inferred ~20 mm if the top matches the sides, from 320 - 291.3 = 28.7 mm total). OSD buttons are five small keys on the underside of the chin at the right end; they face down, not sideways, so a centre-seam bridge does not foul them on the right-hand monitor (they would be at the outer end anyway).

SIDE EDGE PROFILE. The vertical side edge is a plain, squared-off plastic band with a small front chamfer, running the full 320 mm height, curved in plan to follow the 1800R arc (the whole housing is curved; the ends are 35 mm forward of the centre). In Sceptre's top-down photo the housing is thinnest at the two ends and swells toward the centre; in the side photo the top edge is a thin sliver and the housing thickens toward the lower half where the rear module lives. ESTIMATE, from a non-orthographic render scaled by the published 320 mm height: the edge band looks on the order of 15-20 mm deep near the top and ~30-40 mm further down where it wraps the panel plus back cover; the published 81-109 mm depth-without-stand is the rear bulge at the centre, not the edge. Treat this as unmeasured — a caliper on the actual edge is the only real number.

REAR HOUSING. Flat matte back cover with (a) a raised chevron/diamond boss across the upper centre carrying two red LED strips, (b) a shallow rectangular boss across the lower centre with the down-facing port strip, vent slots, and the neck socket, (c) the 75x75 VESA holes sitting in an indentation behind a rubber cover (Sceptre ships a steel adapter plate and four spacers; VIVO's adapter brings the screen ~7.6 mm forward). The cover tapers to the edges, so the last ~40-60 mm at each end (ESTIMATE from the top-down photo) is just panel + thin back cover with no boss — a clip has a smooth curved rear surface to bear on there, but no feature to hook into.

WHERE A CLIP CAN GRIP. Realistic grip points on the inner edge: (1) a C-clip wrapping the side edge band front-to-back — front lip must stay on the black border, i.e. under ~6-8 mm, or it covers pixels; rear lip bears on the tapered back cover; (2) the top edge, same wrap, thin sliver — likely the least deep section; (3) the bottom chin, the deepest and strongest part of the front frame, and the OSD keys are at the far end so a bridge under the inner corner is clear; (4) NOT the VESA — it is under the stand neck at the centre, 350 mm from the seam. Both monitors' tilt hinges are at the centre neck, so a rigid bridge at the seam also has to carry whatever tilt mismatch exists (published tilt ranges differ by variant: +3/-10, +5/-10, +5/-15).

ARC GEOMETRY FOR A CONTINUOUS 1800R PAIR. Each housing subtends 2 x 11.3 deg; placed edge-to-edge on one 1800R circle the inner side faces are parallel to each other only if both are the same model with the same edge chamfer; the front tangent planes meet at 157.4 deg. Because the B30 (left) is a different model, its side band depth and chamfer are not known to match — measure both before designing a symmetric clip.

Whether the published 27.8 in width is the chord or the arc length of the curved housing (affects per-side overhang by ~2 mm).

Whether the C305W-2560UN (85 Hz) also names itself P30: one EDID sample carries a 48-75 Hz range that fits either its HDMI port or an HDMI 1.4 port on the 200 Hz models; unconfirmed.
Panel maker/part number (29.5 in VA 2560x1080 1800R): not published.

edge_geometry_notes: Nothing about the side-edge profile is published for any C305 model; everything below beyond the width/height/depth rows is read off Sceptre's own product renders (galleries product_id=1363 for the C305W-2560UN1 and 1150 for the C305W-2560UN, which share the housing design) and is an ESTIMATE to be caliper-checked. (1) Front: a thin dark rim on the top and both side edges, sitting a millimetre or two proud of the panel face, plus an inner inactive black border; the whole side border is bounded by (706.6-690)/2 = 8.3 mm from housing edge to first pixel. The bottom is a wide dark-grey chin (SCEPTRE logo centred) roughly 20-24 mm tall, with lighter-grey chamfered end caps at both ends in the 2560UN1 render, speaker grilles on its underside near each end, and ventilation slots on the top edge near each end. (2) Side (short) edge: a flat, near-vertical face; in the top-down render the housing is thin at the ends and thick in the middle, i.e. the ends look ~20-25 mm front-to-back versus ~45-55 mm at the central electronics/VESA bulge; the rear cover meets the end face through a rearward facet/chamfer rather than a square corner. The published 93.7 mm 'depth without stand' is a bounding box that includes ~35 mm of 1800R sagitta, so it is NOT the edge thickness. (3) Rear: two raised vertical 'wing' panels about a quarter of the width in from each end, each carrying a blue LED strip; a flatter recessed field between them with the logo; the outermost ~40-50 mm at each end is a plain flat slab — the natural place for a rear jaw of a clip. (4) Keep-outs on the RIGHT edge of this monitor (the inner edge if it is the left screen): the five OSD buttons sit on the rear face at the lower right corner facing backward, and the port strip is right of centre on the rear; a clip that wraps the rear near the bottom-right corner will foul the buttons. (5) The two monitors are different housings even though the panels match: the P30/C305B-200UN family has a V-shaped stand, red chevron LEDs, and OSD buttons on the underside of the front chin (right side), so the connector's two halves must be modelled to two different edge profiles — measure both. (6) Curvature: each 1800R screen subtends 2 x 11.05° over the active width; for a continuous arc the two chassis must be held at 22.6° to each other, with inner edge faces coplanar (radial), and the seam gap is whatever the bezel rims plus clearance leave — ~2 x 8.3 mm of dead border at minimum.

edge_geometry_notes: Nothing about the side-edge profile is published by Sceptre; what follows comes from Sceptre's own spec tables, the user manual, and inspection of Sceptre's product-gallery photos (downloaded and viewed; label crops enlarged 4x). Overall envelope, both chassis: 706-707 mm wide chord, 320-321 mm tall, 94-109 mm deep without stand (Sceptre publishes both 3.69 in and 4.3 in for what appears to be the same red-V housing, so measure). Active area is 690 x 291 mm on both (EDID and 0.2697 mm pitch agree), so the housing adds only ~8-10 mm per side beyond the picture and ~29 mm total top+bottom; DisplayNinja calls the visible black border ~1/4 in. Curve: 1800R gives a 33-35 mm bow, so each inner edge sits ~34 mm in front of its screen centre and each monitor subtends ~22.5 deg of the circle; a continuous arc needs the two centre normals ~22.5 deg apart, i.e. an included angle of ~157.5 deg at the seam, not a straight-line butt joint. Depth is not uniform: the side views show thin tapering ends and a thick central bulge behind the stand mount/VESA area, so a clip cannot assume the 94/109 mm depth exists at the edge - the edge is far thinner (unmeasured). Rear near VESA is a recess ('indentation'), not a flat plate: the stand fixes with one M4x12 screw under a rubber cover and Sceptre ships an X-shaped steel adapter to create a 75x75 M4x10 mount. Rear housings differ between the two: the red-V chassis (P30 by EDID = C305B-200UN family) has a raised V facet at top centre with red LED strips, downward-facing ports in a recessed bay at bottom centre-right, vents bottom left/right, and front-facing OSD buttons at the lower-right of the bottom bezel; the blue-strip chassis (B30 by EDID = C305W-2560UN1; also the 2019 C305W-2560UN whose label says P30) has a three-facet back with vertical blue LED strips in the seams and SIX rear-facing OSD buttons on the lower rear corner that corresponds to the monitor's right-hand edge as viewed from the front - on a left-hand B30 that is the inner edge, so anything wrapping the rear of that edge low down will collide with the buttons. Both have speaker slots in the bottom bezel and a wider bottom bezel than sides/top; side bezels are 'edgeless' style (thin plastic lip plus inactive panel border). Where a clip could grip, given the above: (1) over the top and bottom edges near the seam, where the housing is thinnest and no buttons/ports live at the top (the bottom bezel carries buttons on the P30 lower-right and speaker slots on both); (2) adhesive/VHB pads on the rear shell wings near the inner edge, which is how every existing commercial and printed connector attaches (ScreenBuddy magnet-hinge, Amazon hinge clips) - the rear wing surfaces are smooth but curved and faceted, so pads need to follow the local surface; (3) a bridge between the two 75x75 X-plates/stand necks, which is the only flat, metal, screw-referenced feature on either monitor. Both stands are tilt-only with published ranges that disagree page-to-page (F1-F5 / B10), so the connector must also equalise tilt or the seam will scissor top-to-bottom. All mm figures for edge thickness, bezel widths, rear taper angle, and button/port positions must be caliper-measured on the user's units; the two published depths differ by 15 mm and the user's P30 could be either housing generation.
unknowns: Which physical chassis each name refers to: 'B30' and 'P30' are EDID names shown by the OS (B30 -> SPT0BC2 100 Hz = C305W-2560UN1; P30 -> SPT0BCC 200 Hz = C305B-200UN family), but Sceptre's photo of the 2019 C305W-2560UN shows a rear label 'Model : P30' while its EDID says 'C305W-2560UN'. Ask the user: max refresh (100 vs 200 Hz), LED colour/shape on the back (blue vertical strips vs red V), stand shape (oval ring vs V/tripod), and where the OSD buttons are (rear vs front).
Exact P30 suffix (C305B-200UN / -200UN1 / -200UNT / -200UN1T / -200UN1T.1): not resolvable from the name; the rear label or box gives it.

Housing depth at the side edges (mm), rear-cover taper angle, rim/lip thickness, and bezel widths (side, top, bottom) in mm: not published anywhere; only 'Ultra Slim', 'Edgeless', and DisplayNinja's '1/4 in black border'.

Published overall depth conflicts: 4.3 in (109 mm) on the C305B-200UN/-200UNT/-200UN1T.1/C308B spec pages and manuals vs 3.69 in (94 mm) on the C305B-200UN1/-200UN1T/C305W-2560UN1 pages and 3.74 in on C305W-2560UN; unknown whether this is two housings or two measuring conventions.
Whether Sceptre's 27.8 in width is the chord or the arc length; changes the per-side margin between 7.9 and 10.0 mm.
Exact positions (from the inner edge) of the rear OSD button row (blue-strip chassis), the downward port bay, the vent grilles, and the speaker slots - only qualitative from photos.
Tilt ranges: published as B10/F3, F5/B10, F10/B3, and B10/F1 across Sceptre pages and manuals; actual range on each unit unknown; both are tilt-only and must be matched for a flush seam.
Dimensions of Sceptre's X-shaped VESA adapter plate and the depth of the stand-mount recess: not published (spec PDF has a photo only).

Whether the two panels' inner edges can physically touch: the housing's outermost side surface (plastic lip vs glass edge) is not described, and the 1800R geometry means the edges meet at ~157.5 deg included angle only if both monitors share one arc centre.

No Sceptre-specific or curved-monitor-specific connector design exists to copy; all found designs assume flat backs (adhesive) or straight top/bottom edges (clips); none states a monitor-thickness range for a 30 in curved unit.

Amazon product-detail tables, Walmart pages, displayspecifications.com, MakerWorld, Printables, Thingiverse, MyMiniFactory and YouTube were blocked (403/bot check) for direct fetch; their contents are cited from search snippets only.
The C305B-FUN200W/FUN200W1 'Nebula' 30 in models are 1500R with a height-adjustable stand and 4.79 in depth; excluded because the user states 1800R, but confirm the user's P30 is not white/Nebula.
